name: Autonomous fleet liability
blurb: Risk transferring from local operation to central infrastructure when navigation is cloud controlled.
summary: Risk transferring from local operation to central infrastructure when navigation is cloud controlled.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A broad exclusion for loss arising from failure, malfunction, or inadequacy of any computer system, software, or electronic data, which would remove most autonomous vehicle claims.
A cyber exclusion that bars coverage for accidents caused by ransomware, hacking, or denial of service attacks on the cloud control platform.
A sublimit for technology errors and omissions that caps coverage for software defects at a fraction of the auto liability limit.
An exclusion for loss of connectivity or telecommunications failure, which would defeat claims when a vehicle loses signal and causes a crash.
A requirement that all software updates be pre approved by the insurer, which could delay critical safety patches and create a coverage gap.
A sublimit for any one event involving multiple vehicles, which would leave the fleet operator exposed to a multi vehicle pileup.
An exclusion for liability arising from the acts or omissions of any cloud service provider, subcontractor, or third party data centre.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Negotiate removal of any broad computer system or software failure exclusion and replace it with a specific exclusion only for intentional acts by the insured.
Add an endorsement confirming that cloud service provider negligence is covered as if it were the insured's own negligence, subject to subrogation rights.
Secure a cyber liability extension that covers third party bodily injury and property damage resulting from a cyber attack on the navigation platform.
Obtain a multi vehicle accident endorsement that removes any per event sublimit and confirms the full per occurrence limit applies regardless of the number of vehicles involved.
Add a software update endorsement that allows emergency safety patches without prior insurer consent, provided the insured notifies the insurer within a set number of days.
Negotiate a connectivity failure endorsement that deems loss of signal or latency to be a covered cause of loss unless the insured failed to maintain required redundancy.
Include a contractual liability extension that covers liability assumed under service agreements with municipalities or logistics customers, up to the policy limit.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Not applicable to a liability placement; business interruption waiting periods apply only to first party coverage for the fleet operator's own loss of income.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Not applicable to this liability exposure; contingent business interruption for customers affected by a fleet outage would require a separate first party policy.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Not applicable to this liability exposure; electronic equipment coverage for onboard sensors and computing hardware would be placed under a separate inland marine or equipment policy.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Not applicable to a pure liability placement; if physical damage to the fleet vehicles is required, it is placed on a separate motor hull policy with its own per occurrence limits.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Primary auto liability limits are typically one million dollars per occurrence, but higher primary limits of five million or ten million are common for autonomous fleets because regulators and large shippers often require them.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based for the core auto liability because bodily injury and property damage from a collision manifest at a specific time and may have long tail claims, while the technology errors and omissions component is typically written on a claims made basis to capture late reported software failures.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess towers are built in layers of five million to twenty five million dollars, with total limits of fifty million to two hundred million dollars depending on fleet size, vehicle mass, and contractual indemnity requirements.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury to pedestrians, cyclists, and occupants of other vehicles when a cloud routing error causes a collision.
Property damage to third party vehicles, buildings, and roadside infrastructure from a fleet vehicle under central control.
Multi vehicle pileups triggered by a single erroneous navigation command broadcast to the entire fleet.
Liability for failure of the cloud platform to maintain safe following distances or lane keeping during peak latency.
Claims alleging negligent design or inadequate testing of the central navigation software.
Liability for privacy breaches if location or telemetry data is exposed and causes harm to individuals.
Third party claims for economic loss, such as business interruption of a logistics customer, when fleet operations halt due to a cloud outage.

underwriter_wants_to_know: Fleet size and vehicle types, including whether they are passenger cars, delivery vans, or heavy trucks, because severity scales with mass and occupancy.
Level of driving automation under SAE definitions, specifically whether the cloud system can override local safety controls.
Identity and contractual terms of the cloud service provider, including service level agreements for latency and uptime.
Redundancy and fail safe design, such as local obstacle avoidance when connectivity drops.
Regulatory approvals and any mandated minimum insurance limits in each operating jurisdiction.
Historical incident data from simulation, closed course testing, and real world deployment.
Contractual liability assumed to passengers, shippers, or municipalities under service agreements.
